name: discretus
alternateName: discretus: A Discrete Mathematics library for Python
description: discretus is a rigorous, production-grade library for discrete mathematics in pure Python. It spans seven foundational domains, namely set theory, mathematical logic, combinatorics, graph theory, number theory, recurrence relations, and abstract algebra, and exposes all of them through a single coherent application programming interface with consistent naming, predictable data structures, and uniform error handling. The computational core depends only on the standard library, so the package installs without a compiler on any platform that runs a supported interpreter, while optional visualization and documentation backends are available as extras. Selected routines can record their intermediate steps, which turns an opaque computation into a narrated derivation suitable for teaching, and many objects render themselves to LaTeX so that a computed structure can travel directly from code into a manuscript.
abstract: A unified, dependency free library for the seven classical domains of discrete mathematics, designed for learners, educators, and practitioners, with exact arithmetic, deterministic behavior, and reproducible randomized routines.

hasPart.name: discretus.core
hasPart.description: Shared abstractions and exact numeric helpers, namely the element protocol, the relation and function bases, the algebraic structure interfaces, exact vectors, matrices, and polynomials, modular arithmetic primitives, the step recorder, and the LaTeX rendering mixin.

hasPart.name: discretus.sets
hasPart.description: Finite sets, bit sets, multisets, ordered sets, interval sets, the set algebra, binary and n-ary relations, closures, equivalence relations with union find, and order theory including posets, lattices, and Hasse diagrams.

hasPart.name: discretus.logic
hasPart.description: Propositional expression trees with a lexer and parser, evaluation, truth tables, normal forms, the Tseitin transformation, Quine McCluskey minimization, Karnaugh maps, DPLL and conflict driven clause learning solvers, DIMACS interchange, predicate logic with quantifier evaluation and unification, and an inference layer.

hasPart.name: discretus.combinatorics
hasPart.description: Counting utilities, classical integer sequences, lazy generators for permutations, combinations, subsets, compositions, partitions, necklaces, and Lyndon words, ranking and unranking, formal power series, Polya enumeration, combinatorial designs, and discrete probability.

hasPart.name: discretus.graphs
hasPart.description: Graph, digraph, multigraph, weighted, bipartite, tree, forest, and hypergraph structures with adjacency and incidence views, traversal and connectivity, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, network flow and matching, coloring, Eulerian and Hamiltonian analysis, structural properties, centrality, and generators.

hasPart.name: discretus.number_theory
hasPart.description: Greatest common divisor routines, modular arithmetic, primality testing, factorization, arithmetic functions, diophantine equations, integer sequences, and cryptographic primitives intended for teaching.

hasPart.name: discretus.recurrences
hasPart.description: Linear recurrence solvers, matrix exponentiation, classical sequences, the Master Theorem, recursion trees, the Akra Bazzi method, nonlinear iteration, and asymptotic growth comparison.

hasPart.name: discretus.algebra
hasPart.description: Groups and group actions, rings and ideals, fields and finite fields, polynomial arithmetic and factorization, exact linear algebra over rings and fields, and algebraic lattices.

hasPart.name: discretus.viz
hasPart.description: Pluggable ASCII, SVG, Graphviz, and matplotlib backends for graphs, Hasse diagrams, lattices, trees, truth tables, Karnaugh maps, matrices, and Venn diagrams.

hasPart.name: discretus.io
hasPart.description: Deterministic readers and writers for GraphML, GML, DIMACS, JSON, CSV, edge lists, adjacency data, and LaTeX export.

hasPart.name: discretus.utils
hasPart.description: Cross cutting helpers for timing, memoization, bit manipulation, formatting, validation, iteration, and seeded randomness.

developmentPractices: Every public routine is annotated and carries a docstring that states its parameters, return value, exceptions, and asymptotic complexity.
Advanced algorithms are cross validated against naive reference implementations on randomized inputs.
Property based tests assert the algebraic laws the documentation claims, for instance the distributive and De Morgan laws.
Randomized routines accept an explicit seed and are deterministic once it is supplied.
Serialization is deterministic, so that the same object always produces byte identical output.
The public interface follows semantic versioning, with deprecations announced at least one minor release before removal.
